lines.text: This octopus can pretend to be eighteen different animals. Last night, on the security cameras, it pretended to be *me.*
I'm the night guard at an aquarium. The mimic octopus is real. It was only discovered in 1998, in Indonesia, and when something scares it, it turns into something dangerous.
Flatten out, and it's a poisonous flatfish. Spread its arms, a lionfish. Hide six arms in the sand, wave two, and it's a *sea snake.*
A few weeks ago, it started doing a new one.
It pulled itself up against the glass. Two arms pressed together, like legs. Two held out at its sides. And it *stood.*
It was copying the only thing it sees every night. Me.
When I walked past, it walked with me. When I checked my watch, it lifted an arm. When I waved, it *waved back.*
Last night I fell asleep in the break room. When I woke up, it was 6 A.M. The tank was empty. The lid was still on.
At 4:10, I walk out of the break room. Down the gallery. Past the tanks. And out the staff door.
It's my uniform. My walk. My little wave to the camera.
But I was asleep at 4:10. And the footprints going out the door are *wet.*
It learned everything it needed from watching me.
And my car is gone from the parking lot.
